Furthermore, Sebi recommends exempting ESG debt securities from these limitations and advocates for the removal of mandatory listing on all previous unlisted debt offerings.

items.title: DLF sells penthouse for Rs 271 cr in luxury housing project in Gurugram
items.summary: Realty major DLF Ltd sold a Gurugram penthouse for Rs 271 crore. This luxury housing project is named 'The Dahlias' and is located in DLF Phase 5. The penthouse sale achieved Rs 1.58 lakh per square foot on super area. DLF expects over Rs 40,000 crore revenue from this project. Demand for luxury apartments has increased significantly across major cities post-COVID.

items.summary: Any move toward higher rates would increase borrowing costs for consumers at a time when affordability pressures are already mounting.

items.title: Festive demand set to lift FMCG growth, but margins face pressure
items.summary: Consumer demand in India is expected to strengthen during the upcoming festive season. Companies face rising input costs and intense competition from quick-commerce platforms. Improving purchasing power supports this positive outlook for consumer spending. However, businesses must adapt to premiumization and digital shifts in consumption. Sustained growth hinges on margin protection and faster innovation strategies.

items.summary: Meta launched Muse Glimmer and plans to release Muse Spark 1.2 weights as Zuckerberg pushes for U.S. leadership in open AI.

items.title: French lender's India treasurer pegs rupee floor near 'fair value' of 96 per dollar
items.summary: The Indian rupee is poised for stability against the dollar throughout this financial year. Initiatives to entice dollar investments and a decline in commodity prices are expected to mitigate risks. With foreign investors returning to Indian equity and debt markets, actions from the central bank should help minimize significant currency fluctuations in the short term. Additionally, Indian bonds could stabilize at a yield of approximately 6.70%.

items.title: India bonds tread water ahead of US, local inflation prints
items.summary: On Monday, Indian government bonds remained stable following last week's increases. The rise in oil prices countered some support from softer economic data from the United States. Traders are eagerly awaiting inflation reports from both India and the U.S., which will significantly influence bond market trends this week. Notably, ultra-long bonds saw a rise, likely driven by value purchases from insurers.

items.title: Russia explores rail link to India to bypass maritime chokepoints
items.summary: Russia is exploring a rail link to India through Central Asia and Iran as an alternative to maritime routes vulnerable to disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz and Bosphorus. The proposal comes amid expanding India-Russia energy and bilateral trade ties.

items.title: Indel Money readies its biggest ever public sale of debt: Bankers
items.summary: Indel Money is set to pursue a remarkable fundraising initiative of up to five billion rupees within this month. This forthcoming public debt offering marks the company's most significant endeavor to date. The bonds will have maturities ranging from 400 days to six years, boasting attractive coupon rates between nine and eleven point five percent. Rated A- by India Ratings, these bonds are expected to close on August thirty-first.

items.summary: Parliament has passed the Taxation and other Laws (Amendment) Bill. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman confirmed UPI will remain free for consumers. The legislation removes the linkage between payment systems and income tax. It also provides legal backing to modify zero-MDR frameworks for digital transactions. The bill aims to attract foreign capital and promote domestic manufacturing.

items.summary: Redevelopment remains central to Mumbai’s real estate landscape, given the city’s limited land availability. It has led to ageing residential societies being transformed into modern, well-planned living spaces in premium areas.

items.summary: Indian institutions in QS World University Rankings grew significantly since NIRF's 2015 launch. The National Institutional Ranking Framework promotes healthy competition among higher education institutes. Applications and unique participating institutions under NIRF have also seen substantial increases. The government supports higher education quality through various schemes and policies. These initiatives aim to improve overall educational quality and research capabilities.

items.summary: Zostel withdrew a new application against Oyo parent PRISM in Delhi High Court. The court dismissed the application as withdrawn, finding it lacked merit. This dismissal follows Zostel's withdrawal of an earlier application on July 8.

items.summary: CREDAI West Bengal welcomes the state government's proposed Standard Operating Procedure for building safety. Developers requested an eight-month extension for project approvals and completion validity. Scrutiny of 585 of 706 identified projects for mandatory audit has been completed. The association assured cooperation with the government in scrutinizing pending projects. This initiative aims to boost investor confidence and restart construction activity.

The partnership supports India's transition towards a more gas-based economy.

items.title: EB-5 Visa: Why timing matters before September 2026
items.summary: To secure legal protection under the EB-5 program, potential investors need to submit their applications by September 30, 2026. This crucial deadline allows for grandfathering under existing laws. Post this date, there will be a significant increase in the minimum investment requirement, effective January 1, 2027. It's essential for families and business owners to weigh these important changes now.

items.title: TRAI directs use of 1601-series for service, transactional calls by utilities, logistics cos
items.summary: TRAI mandates a new 1601 number series for transactional calls by other sectors. This initiative aims to separate these calls from sensitive BFSI and government communications. Utilities, courier, and logistics firms will initially adopt the dedicated 1601 number series. This move will help combat impersonation by fraudsters using regular ten-digit numbers. Telecom operators must complete onboarding eligible entities within ninety days.

items.summary: Indian inspectors seized approximately eighteen thousand boxes of Diageo liquor bottles. These bottles allegedly lacked required markings for safe recycled plastic usage. Diageo India confirmed the regulatory action, stating some bottles are quarantined. The food standards regulator is increasingly strict on labelling and compliance issues. This action follows recent bans on Diageo brands for misleading declarations.

items.title: Project Sudarsan: How Sebi is using AI to police finfluencers with 60% of investors trusting their advice

items.title: India's Russian crude imports hit record for second straight month
items.summary: India's Russian crude oil imports reached a record in July, increasing by 2.1 percent. This surge was primarily fueled by smaller import terminals across the country. Larger terminals like Jamnagar saw stable volumes, while Paradip experienced a decline. India remains a significant buyer of Russian fossil fuels, second only to China. This trend highlights India's continued reliance on discounted Russian energy supplies.

items.title: Sanjiv Goenka-led RPSG arm to acquire 1.4 GW solar projects from ReNew for Rs 4,859 crore
items.summary: In a move that signifies a major leap towards sustainability, CESE Ltd, under the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group, is acquiring six solar projects, consolidating a total capacity of 1.4 GWp at a cost of Rs 4,859 crore. Following this acquisition, Purvah Green Power’s capacity will reach 4.8 GWp, aligning perfectly with the group's goal to develop a robust 10 GW renewable energy platform.

items.title: Rupee weakness cushioned by central bank intervention, shorts grow wary
items.summary: The Indian rupee ended the day with minimal fluctuations, influenced primarily by oil market dynamics and moves from the central bank. State-owned banks reportedly intervened by supplying dollars on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India, helping to buffer the currency against rising oil costs and global tensions. Traders are taking a measured approach, with a noted resistance threshold at 96.

Reduced rainfall in key states has raised concerns about next year's sugar output. The government might allow corn and rice for ethanol to maintain its blending program.

items.title: India, South Africa-led SACU group may ink terms of reference for negotiating trade pact on Aug 12
items.summary: India and the SACU group will sign terms of reference for trade talks. Negotiations for a preferential trade agreement are expected to begin soon. South Africa is India's largest trading partner within the SACU bloc. Bilateral trade between India and South Africa saw a dip last fiscal year. Other SACU members like Botswana and Namibia show growing trade with India.

items.title: India expands LNG sourcing from 6 to 15 countries to cut supply risks: Govt
items.summary: India has nearly trebled its liquefied natural gas suppliers to fifteen countries. The nation also broadened its crude oil sourcing network to forty-one countries. This diversification reduces dependence on any single supplier or transit route. India is also expanding its strategic petroleum storage capacity to manage supply shocks. These measures strengthen the country's energy supply resilience against disruptions.

items.title: Has Dalal Street's near term outlook improved? HSBC lists 4 headwinds, 3 tailwinds to watch out for
items.summary: HSBC Mutual Fund remains constructive on Indian equities, citing improving earnings, private capex, policy support and potential trade deals. However, elevated commodity prices, weak global growth, a below-normal monsoon and slower government capex remain key risks for markets.

items.title: India's peak power demand rises 12% in April-June, evening supply gap widens to 3,045 MW: Govt
items.summary: India's peak electricity demand rose 12 per cent from April to June over the same period last year. An all-time high of 270.8 gigawatts was recorded in May. June saw an evening supply gap of over three thousand megawatts.

items.title: Gold, silver import duty hike: Govt nets ₹10,463 crore in revenue between May 13 and August 2

items.title: Retailers’ cooking gas losses dip in August, but government dues top Rs 59,000 crore
items.summary: Fuel retailers' revenue loss on subsidized LPG narrowed to Rs 188 per cylinder in August. This marks a sharp decrease from the Rs 500 loss reported in the previous month. The government paid Rs 30,000 crore to clear past subsidy dues. However, outstanding payments to retailers still exceed Rs 59,000 crore. This compensation mechanism shields households from price volatility.

items.title: Bharat Forge shares plunge 9% after firm posts Rs 90 crore Q1 net loss on exceptional items, revenue rises 19%
items.summary: Bharat Forge shares plunged nearly 9% after the company reported an Rs 89.89 crore consolidated net loss in Q1 FY27, compared with a Rs 284 crore profit a year earlier. One-time restructuring and VRS costs of Rs 358 crore hurt earnings. Revenue rose 19%, while defence revenue surged 87%, despite lower margins.

Import duties on gold and silver were raised to fifteen percent in May. This move aimed to curb discretionary imports and conserve foreign exchange reserves. Authorities also seized 161 kg of smuggled gold and made arrests.

items.title: Centre proposes to curb powers of states to tax minerals
items.summary: The central government is poised to restrict state authority concerning taxation on mining activities. This initiative aims to enhance the national viability of mining operations, as previous overly burdensome taxes deterred mineral extraction. Following a 2024 Supreme Court ruling that permitted states to add taxes, the proposed legislation aspires to introduce a standardized and fair financial framework for the mining industry.

Investors awaited key economic data and monetary-policy signals, while strong corporate earnings and expectations of lower U.S. borrowing costs supported sentiment. Energy and technology stocks gained, but geopolitical risks and elevated crude prices limited broader market gains.

items.title: Elon Musk vs Michael Burry: World's richest man says AI internet traffic will outpace humans, market expert asks who is paying

items.title: Govt considering raising CCEA approval threshold for FDI proposals to Rs 15,000 crore: Sources
items.summary: The government is considering raising the FDI approval threshold for proposals requiring CCEA clearance to Rs 15,000 crore from Rs 5,000 crore, in a move aimed at improving ease of doing business. It is also weighing easier downstream investment norms to boost foreign inflows, job creation and investment, sources said.

items.title: Households in India, other Asia-Pacific regions highly vulnerable to El Nino-driven price shocks: S&P
items.summary: Asia-Pacific economies face rising prices and weather shocks from El Nino. Reduced rainfall and climate disruption will affect agricultural output and food inflation. Countries are strengthening food reserves and water management to mitigate these impacts. India holds significant food grain buffers to manage potential food shocks. Proactive policies will limit damage from the developing El Nino episode.

items.title: More than half of India's AI workers expect layoffs soon, but engineers appear to be the least concerned, finds survey
items.summary: A survey of 1,552 professionals reveals that more than half of AI and ML workers foresee layoffs within 3-6 months. In contrast, only 24% of engineers anticipate job cuts, suggesting they feel safer despite AI advancement. Details here.
